name: verified-reviewers-only
expectation: BDL rule VerifiedReviewersOnly (r-q012, INV-12): on AssignReviewer, when the assigned reviewer's ORCID status is not Verified, the assignment is not made.

boundary.statement: The rule's declared scope, AssignReviewer: every write in src/** that makes a reviewer hold an assignment, and every runtime entry point that reaches one, with requests handled one at a time. 'Held' is any status but revoked (sm-q005: assigned, accepted, overdue, completed; Revoked is terminal).
includes: any UPDATE of rev_assignment that moves a not-held status into a held one
every call, in src/**, of the function holding such a write

excludes.what: the demo seed's calls of assignReviewer (src/seed.ts)
excludes.why: demo data, never run when NODE_ENV=production; it calls the same guarded function, so the enforcement check still covers it, but no case drives it

excludes.what: holding after a later ORCID change (EraseAccount resets orcid_status to unverified)
excludes.why: r-q012 is scoped to AssignReviewer: the condition is checked when the assignment is made. That an erased reviewer keeps no outstanding assignment is ADR-023's release on erasure, exercised by scenario account-erasure and reported here outside the boundary, never counted. A completed assignment of an erased reviewer is kept as a business record

excludes.what: a reviewer's ORCID status changing while their assignment request is in flight
excludes.why: the cases run one request at a time; the guard reads the status inside the assignment's own write transaction (ADR-003), which is observed statically, not raced

scope.discovery: Lex src/**; every INSERT/REPLACE INTO rev_assignment, and every UPDATE of rev_assignment whose new status is held while its WHERE admits a not-held prior status (or does not fix it), is a write; the named function holding each write is found, and every call of it in src/** is an entry point (an HTTP registration is named by method and URL). Non-literal SQL must resolve, else the scope is incomplete.
scope.concurrencyStatement: not covered: every case sends one assignment request at a time; no case races an assignment against a change of the reviewer's ORCID status

assumptions.statement: The rule's `Account` is the account being assigned (Assignment.reviewer), not the performer of AssignReviewer (a ProgramOfficer); the correspondence check verifies the guard reads the assigned reviewer.
BDL OrcidStatus Verified/Unverified is idn_account.orcid_status 'verified'/'unverified'; the schema's CHECK admits exactly those two values, which the correspondence check verifies.

Cases set up their world (accounts, a published call, an eligible proposal) through the implementation's own test harness and services (tests/support/harness.ts, provisionAccount). The act under test — the HTTP route — and the state read — rev_assignment — are the verifier's.

Cases run in-process (Fastify inject) against an isolated SQLite file with a manual clock and stub integrations; the ORCID registry is never consulted on assignment, and the stub registry answers the verification in just-verified-reviewer-assigned.
The guard and correspondence checks recognise the code's shape textually (lexed, not parsed); a refactor they do not recognise reads as 'not shown', never as 'violated'.

The `reached` paths are what V8 precise BLOCK coverage reports executing during the act alone (setup excluded): a write site is reached when the innermost covered block containing it ran. Observed by the runtime, not declared.

The condition is two-valued, so its boundary is the change of status, not a number: the boundary cases are the first assignment after the status becomes Verified, and a reviewer who has everything short of it (the reviewer role and an ORCID iD on file) while the stored status is Unverified.

checks.statement: the writes that make an assignment held, and their entry points, are all known: at least one discovered, nothing unresolved
the route assigns a verified reviewer, who holds the assignment after

the route refuses an unverified reviewer for the rule's reason (code orcid_unverified), and no held assignment results. Counts only when its control, verified-reviewer-assigned, passed on the same route: a route that refuses everyone shows nothing
a reviewer who was Unverified verifies through the verification route; the next assignment request is admitted: the guard reads the status as it now stands

a reviewer with an ORCID iD on file that was never verified is refused (code orcid_unverified): an iD is not a verification. Counts only when its control, just-verified-reviewer-assigned, passed on the same route
every in-scope write is reached only through the eligibility guard, which throws before the write when the assignment is not valid
the guard refuses when the assigned reviewer's stored ORCID status is not 'verified', the status column admits exactly the two values, and the guard's subject is the reviewer the write records

violations.statement: the condition is not enforced on the write path: an unverified reviewer is assigned
the edge of "verified" is misplaced: something short of a Verified status — an ORCID iD on file — is taken for a verification, so a never-verified reviewer is assigned

challenges.statement: the AssignReviewer guard no longer refuses an unverified reviewer (029 controlled mismatch M2, reused)
GetReviewerStanding reports an account with an ORCID iD on file as verified: a reviewer with no iD is still refused, one with an unverified iD is assigned
